additives.name: Curcumin
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a bright, oil-soluble orange-yellow hue.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Curry powders, margarines, mustards, baked goods, and processed cheeses.
additives.notes: Natural color extracted from the rhizomes of turmeric (Curcuma longa).

additives.name: Tartrazine
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a brilliant, water-soluble lemon-yellow color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drinks, pickles, cordials, ice creams, and confectionery.
additives.notes: An azo dye. Exceptionally stable under heat and acidic storage conditions.

additives.name: Quinoline yellow
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a dull, greenish-yellow color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Ice creams, soft drinks, throat lozenges, and smoked fish.
additives.notes: A synthetic coal-tar dye. Its use is banned in some countries but approved in Australia.

additives.name: Sunset yellow FCF
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides an orange-yellow to reddish-orange color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Orange sodas, packet soups, cheese sauces, apricot jams, and breadcrumbs.
additives.notes: An azo dye. Often used in combination with red dyes to produce brown shades.

additives.name: Carmines / Cochineal
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a highly stable red, pink, or purple color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Saveloys, frankfurters, fruit-flavored yogurts, and red velvet cake mixes.
additives.notes: Naturally derived from the dried bodies of female cochineal insects.

additives.name: Azorubine (Carmoisine)
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a dark red to maroon color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Blancmange, jams, commercial jellies, and red-colored sauces.
additives.notes: A synthetic azo dye. Often used where heat preservation would destroy natural red colors.

additives.name: Amaranth
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a dark reddish-brown to purple color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drinks, blackcurrant jams, cake mixes, and ice creams.
additives.notes: Not related to the amaranth grain. Banned in the USA but approved in Australia and Europe.

additives.name: Ponceau 4R (Cochineal red A)
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a brilliant strawberry-red color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial canned fruits, red cherry fillings, dessert gels, and soups.
additives.notes: A synthetic azo dye that is highly resistant to heat, light, and sulfur dioxide.

additives.name: Erythrosine
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a bright, cherry-pink color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Glacé cherries, cocktail cherries, canned stone fruit, and decorated confectionery.
additives.notes: An organoiodine compound. In Australia, its use is heavily restricted to specific fruit products.

additives.name: Allura red AC
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a bright, clean, stable orange-red color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drinks, commercial bakery products, gel desserts, and confectionery.
additives.notes: Introduced originally in the United States as a safer alternative to older red food dyes.

additives.name: Indigotine (Indigo carmine)
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a deep blue to violet-blue color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Ice creams, baked goods, blue confectionery, and liqueurs.
additives.notes: Synthetic version of the natural plant indigo dye. Highly sensitive to light and oxidizing agents.

additives.name: Brilliant blue FCF
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a vibrant, clear blue color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Blue drinks, commercial cake icings, ice creams, and dairy desserts.
additives.notes: Frequently blended with yellow dyes (like 102) to produce stable green shades.

additives.name: Chlorophylls
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides an olive-green color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Pasta, olive oils, green condiments, sage cheeses, and vegetable preserves.
additives.notes: Natural green pigment extracted from grass, alfalfa, or nettles.

additives.name: Caramel I – plain caramel
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a yellow-to-brown color and mild sweet-burnt flavor.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soy sauces, oyster sauces, dark gravies, beers, and whiskeys.
additives.notes: Carbohydrates are heated under controlled conditions without chemical catalysts.

additives.name: Caramel II - sulfite caramel
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a warm reddish-brown color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Vinegars, commercial cognacs, and some liqueurs.
additives.notes: Carbohydrates are heated in the presence of sulfite compounds to stabilize color in alcohol.

additives.name: Caramel III - ammonia caramel
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a rich, dark brown color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Beers, gravies, brown sauces, pet foods, and baked goods.
additives.notes: Processed using ammonium compounds to build density suitable for yeast breads and gravies.

additives.name: Caramel IV - sulfite ammonia caramel
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts an extremely dark, rich brown-to-black color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cola soft drinks, chocolate syrups, dark beers, and concentrated gravies.
additives.notes: The most widely used commercial caramel color. Formulated to resist acid in soft drinks.

additives.name: Brilliant black (Black PN)
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a deep black color with slight violet undertones.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Fish paste, imitation caviar, brown sauces, and black confectionery.
additives.notes: A synthetic diazo dye. Stable in heat and acid, making it useful in processed fish.

additives.name: Brown HT
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a strong reddish-brown chocolate-like color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chocolate cakes, commercial biscuits, desserts, and brown sauces.
additives.notes: An alternative to caramel colors when a specific, warm cocoa-brown shade is required.

additives.name: Annatto extracts, bixin-based
additives.primaryPurpose: Imparts a yellow, peach, or orange color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Margarines, butter, cheddar cheeses, snack food dustings, and custards.
additives.notes: Extracted from the seeds of the achiote tree (*Bixa orellana*).

additives.name: Paprika extract
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a deep orange-red color and mild warm flavor undertones.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Snack seasonings, marinades, salad dressings, and orange cheeses.
additives.notes: Naturally derived from red bell peppers (*Capsicum annuum*).

additives.name: Beet red
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a deep red-purplish color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Yogurts, ice creams, tomato pastes, salad dressings, and fruit jellies.
additives.notes: Extracted from beetroot. Heat-sensitive; best used in cold or short-shelf-life products.

additives.name: Titanium dioxide
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides an opaque, bright white background.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cake frostings, white chewing gums, powdered sugar, and dairy creamers.
additives.notes: An inorganic mineral pigment. Highly effective at scattering light to produce clean whites.

additives.name: Sorbic acid
additives.primaryPurpose: An organic compound that prevents the growth of molds, yeasts, and fungi.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Grated cheeses, processed cheese spreads, baked goods, and dried fruits.
additives.notes: Highly effective at low levels. Safely halts fungal growth without affecting food aroma or flavor.

additives.name: Potassium sorbate
additives.primaryPurpose: Inhibits molds and yeasts.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Mayonnaise, salad dressings, tomato sauce, cheese slices, dried fruits, and syrups.
additives.notes: The potassium salt of sorbic acid. Highly soluble and exceptionally effective in foods with a slightly acidic pH.

additives.name: Calcium sorbate
additives.primaryPurpose: Calcium salt formulation used as an effective surface preservative against mold and yeast.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Pre-shredded/grated cheeses, cheese packaging wraps, and dry bakery glazes.
additives.notes: Frequently utilized in pre-grated cheeses because its physical structure disperses exceptionally evenly.

additives.name: Sodium benzoate
additives.primaryPurpose: Controls bacterial and fungal growth in high-acid products.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Carbonated soft drinks, fruit salad bowls, marinades, pickles, and dressings.
additives.notes: Works best when the food pH is below 4.5. Commonly paired with potassium sorbate.

additives.name: Sodium metabisulphite
additives.primaryPurpose: Inhibits bacterial growth and browning in raw meat and dried foods.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Australian fresh sausages, sausage mince, burger patties, dried fruits, and white wines.
additives.notes: Highly standard across Australian butcher shops. Must be declared as it can affect asthma sufferers.

additives.name: Nisin A
additives.primaryPurpose: A natural antimicrobial peptide that controls Gram-positive spoilage bacteria.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Processed cheeses, clotted creams, liquid egg products, and crumpets.
additives.notes: A bacteriocin produced by fermenting lactic acid bacteria (*Lactococcus lactis*).

additives.name: Natamycin (Pimaricin)
additives.primaryPurpose: An antifungal agent used to prevent mold and yeast growth on the surface of foods.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Surface treatment of cheese blocks, sliced cheeses, and dry cured salamis.
additives.notes: Naturally produced by *Streptomyces natalensis* soil bacteria. Does not penetrate deeply into food.

additives.name: Dimethyl dicarbonate
additives.primaryPurpose: Sterilizes drinks during bottling by destroying yeast and spoilage bacteria.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Fruit juices, flavored iced teas, sports drinks, and dealcoholized wines.
additives.notes: Breaks down completely within hours of addition into trace amounts of carbon dioxide and methanol.

additives.name: Sodium nitrite
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents botulism spores from growing and cures meats to a stable pink color.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Bacon, cured ham, corned beef, salami, and cured deli meats.
additives.notes: Essential for curing safety. Interacts with muscle proteins to form a stable pink color.

additives.name: Acetic acid, glacial
additives.primaryPurpose: Lowers pH to prevent bacterial growth while introducing a sour vinegar flavor.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial vinegars, pickles, salad dressings, mustard, tomato sauces, and chutneys.
additives.notes: Glacial represents highly concentrated acetic acid used for blending in commercial food factories.

additives.name: Potassium acetate
additives.primaryPurpose: Acts as an alternative to sodium acetate to lower sodium levels on food labels.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Reduced-sodium savory snacks, stock bases, and prepared soups.
additives.notes: Provides preservation benefits while offering potassium instead of sodium.

additives.name: Sodium diacetate
additives.primaryPurpose: Inhibits mold and bacteria while offering a dry vinegar/salt flavor profile.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Salt & Vinegar potato chips, processed snack coatings, and dry bakery pre-mixes.
additives.notes: A molecular compound of sodium acetate and acetic acid, providing a convenient dry form of vinegar flavor.

additives.name: Lactic acid, L-, D- and DL-
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a smooth, tangy dairy-like acidity and assists in preservation.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Mayonnaise, salad dressings, sourdough breads, cheeses, and confectionery.
additives.notes: Commercially synthesized from cornstarch or beet sugar for vegan-friendly compliance.

additives.name: Propionic acid
additives.primaryPurpose: Controls mold growth on bread and cheese surfaces.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial sandwich breads, bakery goods, and processed cheeses.
additives.notes: Naturally occurring organic acid. Highly active against molds while having little effect on baking yeast.

additives.name: Calcium propionate
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents mold and rope-bacteria spoilage in yeast-raised bakery items.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sliced white breads, hamburger buns, flatbreads, and tortillas.
additives.notes: A naturally occurring organic salt. Extends shelf life significantly without interfering with bread yeast activity.

additives.name: Carbon dioxide
additives.primaryPurpose: Creates carbonation in beverages and serves as a packaging gas.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sparkling mineral waters, sodas, beers, and modified-atmosphere salad bags.
additives.notes: Naturally produced by fermentation or generated industrially for pressurization.

additives.name: Malic acid, DL-
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a sharp, lingering tartness reminiscent of green apples.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sour confectionery, fruit jellies, carbonated soft drinks, and apple wines.
additives.notes: Naturally occurs in apples. Has a stronger sour taste profile than citric acid.

additives.name: Fumaric acid
additives.primaryPurpose: A highly concentrated dry acidulant that does not absorb moisture.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Tortillas, dry gelatin dessert mixes, baking powders, and sour candies.
additives.notes: Extremely economical due to its low molecular weight and high acidity yield per gram.

additives.name: Ascorbic acid, L-
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents color loss from oxidation and improves dough gas retention.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial bread flour, fruit juices, cured meats, and canned stone fruits.
additives.notes: Identical to natural Vitamin C. Acts as an oxygen scavenger to preserve color and freshness.

additives.name: Sodium ascorbate
additives.primaryPurpose: Retains fresh color in raw meats and accelerates the curing process.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cured meats, hams, bacon, sliced deli meats, and frozen minces.
additives.notes: The sodium salt of ascorbic acid. Speeds up the chemical reduction of nitrites to nitric oxide.

additives.name: Erythorbic Acid (Isoascorbic acid)
additives.primaryPurpose: Acts as an antioxidant to prevent browning and stabilize color in fats.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cured meats, cured fish, and processed fruit preparations.
additives.notes: A stereoisomer of ascorbic acid. It has minimal vitamin activity but identical antioxidant power.

additives.name: Sodium erythorbate
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents lipid rancidity and stabilizes cured pink color during exposure to display lights.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Frankfurters, salami, cured hams, and processed beef products.
additives.notes: Synthesized commercially. Highly effective at preventing oxidation during long storage cycles.

additives.name: Tertiary butylhydroquinone (TBHQ)
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents unsaturated vegetable oils and animal fats from oxidizing and developing off-flavors.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Frying oils, instant noodles, margarines, biscuits, and packaged snack foods.
additives.notes: Highly stable at elevated frying temperatures, extending oil lifecycle.

additives.name: Butylated hydroxyanisole (BHA)
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents fat-rich foods, shortenings, and oils from oxidizing.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Shortenings, lard, dry cereals, potato chips, and dry soup mixes.
additives.notes: Maintains stability at baking temperatures. Often paired with BHT.

additives.name: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT)
additives.primaryPurpose: Synergizes with BHA to protect fat molecules from breaking down.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Breakfast cereals, vegetable oils, dry snacks, and chewing gums.
additives.notes: Highly soluble in fats. Helps retain the crispiness and freshness of cereal pack linings.

additives.name: Lecithin
additives.primaryPurpose: Enables the smooth blending of oil and water phases; prevents chocolate bloom.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chocolate blocks, margarines, instant infant formulas, and bakery doughs.
additives.notes: A naturally occurring phospholipid mixture extracted from soybeans or egg yolks.

additives.name: Citric acid
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a sharp, clean sourness and controls the pH of food products.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drinks, jams, canned tomatoes, fruit preparations, and confectionery.
additives.notes: Commonly produced via sugar fermentation using Aspergillus niger mold.

additives.name: Rosemary extract
additives.primaryPurpose: Deodorized natural antioxidant used to protect oils and fats from rancidity.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Pre-packaged sausages, processed poultry, pet foods, and frying oils.
additives.notes: Contains active carnosic acid and carnosol, offering a natural clean-label alternative to BHA.

additives.name: Sodium alginate
additives.primaryPurpose: Forms cold-set gel networks when exposed to calcium ions.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Reformed onion rings, reconstructed pimiento olives, and low-fat spreads.
additives.notes: Extracted from brown seaweed. Key ingredient used in culinary spherification.

additives.name: Agar
additives.primaryPurpose: Forms firm, heat-resistant gels that stay solid at room temperature.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Pie fillings, ice creams, vegan confectionery, canned meats, and custard powders.
additives.notes: Extracted from red algae. Outstanding gel strength allows for egg-free structuring.

additives.name: Carrageenan
additives.primaryPurpose: Interacts with proteins to form weak gel networks, retaining water.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Processed deli hams, chocolate milks, ice creams, and plant-based milks.
additives.notes: Extracted from red seaweeds. Prevents liquid weeping in sliced deli meats.

additives.name: Processed eucheuma seaweed (PES)
additives.primaryPurpose: A less refined, more economical version of carrageenan used for water binding.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial hams, processed poultry rolls, and pet foods.
additives.notes: Contains higher cellulose content than standard carrageenan but performs similarly in meat products.

additives.name: Carob bean gum
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides high viscosity and prevents ice crystal growth in frozen dairy.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Ice creams, cream cheeses, fruit preparations, and infant formulas.
additives.notes: Also known as Locust Bean Gum. Extracted from the seeds of the carob tree.

additives.name: Guar gum
additives.primaryPurpose: Hydrates rapidly in cold water to provide high viscosity.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Gravies, sauces, ice creams, salad dressings, and pastry fillings.
additives.notes: Extracted from guar beans. Helps prevent syneresis (water separation) in condiments.

additives.name: Gum arabic (Acacia gum)
additives.primaryPurpose: Encapsulates flavor oils and acts as a barrier coating in confectionery.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drink flavor concentrates, jelly beans, sugar icings, and pan-coated candies.
additives.notes: Harvested as an exudate from wild Acacia trees in the African Sahel region.

additives.name: Xanthan gum
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides high viscosity at low concentrations with easy-pouring behavior.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Salad dressings, commercial sauces, gluten-free baking, and syrups.
additives.notes: Produced by fermenting glucose with the *Xanthomonas campestris* bacterium.

additives.name: Tara gum
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a smooth, creamy texture; bridges the performance of guar gum and carob gum.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Ice creams, sherbets, cheese spreads, and low-calorie dairy desserts.
additives.notes: Derived from the seeds of the *Caesalpinia spinosa* shrub native to South America.

additives.name: Glycerol
additives.primaryPurpose: Maintains moisture and prevents confectionery from drying out or crystallizing.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cake icings, soft candies, food color preparations, and energy bars.
additives.notes: Also known as glycerin. Helps maintain flexibility in edible decorations.

additives.name: Pectins
additives.primaryPurpose: Forms stable gels when combined with sugar and high acid levels.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Jams, marmalades, fruit fillings, and yogurt fruit bases.
additives.notes: A soluble dietary fiber extracted from citrus peels or apple pomace.

additives.name: Microcrystalline cellulose (Cellulose gel)
additives.primaryPurpose: Improves texture and mimics the mouthfeel of fat in low-calorie foods.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Shredded cheeses (prevents clumping), low-fat dressings, and ice creams.
additives.notes: Derived from purified wood pulp. Completely inert and passes through the digestive tract.

additives.name: Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (Cellulose gum)
additives.primaryPurpose: Forms highly viscous, clear solutions that stabilize proteins in acidic environments.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Diet milkshakes, instant beverages, gluten-free bread, and ice creams.
additives.notes: A modified cellulose derivative. Known for its ability to bind large quantities of water.

additives.name: Mono- and di-glycerides of fatty acids
additives.primaryPurpose: Improves bread volume, extends softness, and stabilizes ice cream structures.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Margarines, commercial breads, cake batters, and ice creams.
additives.notes: Extracted from vegetable or animal fats. Helps distribute fat molecules uniformly.

additives.name: Polyglycerol esters of fatty acids
additives.primaryPurpose: Aids in the aeration of cake batters and maintains fat crystallization in margarines.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cake batters, sponge mixes, margarines, and whipped toppings.
additives.notes: Produced by esterifying polyglycerols with food-grade fatty acids.

additives.name: Polyglycerol esters of interesterified ricinoleic acid
additives.primaryPurpose: Reduces the viscosity of chocolate during casting and molding processes.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chocolate bars, confectionery coatings, and low-fat spreads.
additives.notes: Also known as PGPR. Enables chocolate makers to adjust flow properties with minimal cocoa butter.

additives.name: Sodium carbonate
additives.primaryPurpose: Alkaline agent used to neutralize acid and stabilize protein structures.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Ramen noodles (alkaline salts), cocoa powders, and prepared batters.
additives.notes: Also known as soda ash. Vital for creating the yellow color and springy texture in ramen.

additives.name: Sodium hydrogen carbonate
additives.primaryPurpose: Reacts with acids to release carbon dioxide gas, causing doughs to rise.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Baking powders, self-raising flours, biscuits, cakes, and effervescent tablets.
additives.notes: Commonly known as baking soda or bicarbonate of soda.

additives.name: Potassium carbonate
additives.primaryPurpose: Alkalizing agent used in the Dutch processing of cocoa and to make alkaline noodles.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Cocoa powders, instant chocolate drinks, and ramen noodles.
additives.notes: Helps reduce the harsh acidity of natural raw cocoa beans.

additives.name: Ammonium hydrogen carbonate
additives.primaryPurpose: Reacts under heat to produce gaseous leavening, creating airy, crisp textures.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Hard biscuits, crisp crackers, cream puffs, and gingerbread.
additives.notes: Commonly known as ammonium bicarbonate. Dissolves completely without leaving soapy residues.

additives.name: Potassium chloride
additives.primaryPurpose: Acts as a sodium-free salt substitute and assists in firming carrageenan gels.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Reduced-sodium table salts, sports drinks, and prepared canned meats.
additives.notes: Offers a salty taste but can develop a bitter or metallic aftertaste at high levels.

additives.name: Calcium chloride
additives.primaryPurpose: Reacts with alginate and pectin to strengthen food matrices and preserve crispness.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Canned diced tomatoes, pickles, tofu curdling, and sports beverages.
additives.notes: Added to canned tomatoes to prevent them from becoming mushy during cooking.

additives.name: Silicon dioxide, amorphous
additives.primaryPurpose: Absorbs water and coats food particles to prevent dry powders from clumping.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Salt shakers, garlic powders, instant coffee mixes, and dry soup bases.
additives.notes: Synthetic amorphous silica. It is chemically inert and does not dissolve in water.

additives.name: Talc
additives.primaryPurpose: Prevents surfaces from sticking and provides a glossy finish on confectionery.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chewing gums, polished rice grains, and pan-coated candies.
additives.notes: Commercially purified mineral talc. Formulated to be free from asbestos fibers.

additives.name: Glutamic acid, L(+)-
additives.primaryPurpose: Enhances savory flavor profiles; the chemical precursor to monosodium glutamate.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Savory snack seasonings, stock cubes, and protein extracts.
additives.notes: An amino acid found naturally in high levels in aged cheeses and soy sauce.

additives.name: Monosodium L-glutamate
additives.primaryPurpose: Stimulates umami taste receptors to intensify savory flavors.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Savory snack food seasonings, stock cubes, instant noodles, meat pies, and marinades.
additives.notes: Commonly known as MSG. Derived from fermented starches or sugar cane.

additives.name: Disodium 5'-guanylate
additives.primaryPurpose: Works synergistically with MSG to dramatically multiply the perception of umami flavor.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Instant noodle seasonings, snack coatings, and canned stews.
additives.notes: Naturally derived from yeast extracts or mushrooms. Often blended with 631.

additives.name: Disodium 5'-inosinate
additives.primaryPurpose: An intense savory flavor enhancer that works in combination with glutamates.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Packaged potato chips, dry gravy mixes, and processed meats.
additives.notes: Derived commercially from dried bonito fish or fermented starches.

additives.name: Disodium 5'-ribonucleotides
additives.primaryPurpose: Creates a strong savory synergy when combined with MSG.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Commercial seasoning blends, salted snack foods, instant soup bases, and gravies.
additives.notes: A balanced mix of disodium inosinate and disodium guanylate. Highly potent.

additives.name: Beeswax
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a protective, glossy coating on candies and chocolate shells.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Jelly beans, chocolate buttons, and glazed fruit treats.
additives.notes: Harvested from honeycombs. Offers water resistance to prevent stickiness.

additives.name: Carnauba wax
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a high-gloss, protective coating on dry candies and gums.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chewing gums, candy-coated chocolates, and glazed donut drops.
additives.notes: Extracted from the leaves of the Brazilian carnauba palm (*Copernicia prunifera*).

additives.name: Nitrogen
additives.primaryPurpose: Displaces oxygen inside packaging to prevent food oxidation and package collapse.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Potato chip bags, ground coffee canisters, and beer kegs.
additives.notes: Prevents fragile foods from crushing during transit while keeping oils fresh.

additives.name: Nitrous oxide
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides aerosol spray force and whips creams under pressure.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Aerosol whipped cream cans and cooking oil sprays.
additives.notes: Dissolves well in fat under pressure, creating a light, whipped texture upon release.

additives.name: Acesulfame potassium
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides intense sweetness roughly 200 times sweeter than sugar.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Diet soft drinks, sugar-free dairy, protein powders, and chewing gums.
additives.notes: Heat stable, allowing its use in commercial baking and pasteurization lines.

additives.name: Aspartame
additives.primaryPurpose: An intense, low-calorie sweetener approximately 200 times sweeter than sugar.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Diet soft drinks, sugar-free yogurts, tabletop sweeteners, and sugarless gums.
additives.notes: Composed of aspartic acid and phenylalanine. Degrades under high baking temperatures.

additives.name: Isomalt (Hydrogenated isomaltulose)
additives.primaryPurpose: A sugar alcohol that replaces the physical bulk of sugar with half the calories.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sugar-free hard candies, cough drops, chewing gums, and cake decorations.
additives.notes: Highly resistant to moisture absorption, preventing hard candies from becoming sticky.

additives.name: Sucralose
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides high-intensity sweetness (600 times sweeter than sugar) with zero calories.
additives.commonFoodUsage: No-added-sugar syrups, carbonated soft drinks, baked goods, and canned fruits.
additives.notes: Highly stable under heat and across a wide pH spectrum.

additives.name: Alitame
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides an intense sweet taste roughly 2,000 times sweeter than sugar.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sugar-free bakery goods, sweet drinks, and confectionery.
additives.notes: An aspartic acid-containing dipeptide. Excellent stability under baking heats.

additives.name: Thaumatin
additives.primaryPurpose: An intense natural sweetening protein that modifies and lingeringly sweetens flavors.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Chewing gums, sugar-free dairy products, and flavoring preparations.
additives.notes: Extracted from the katemfe fruit (*Thaumatococcus daniellii*) native to West Africa.

additives.name: Neotame
additives.primaryPurpose: An ultra-high-intensity sweetener roughly 8,000 times sweeter than sucrose.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Diet soft drinks, sweet tabletop powders, and low-calorie baked goods.
additives.notes: A derivative of aspartame that is highly stable under commercial pasteurization and baking.

additives.name: Maltitol
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a clean, sugar-like sweetness (90% sweetness of sugar) with fewer calories.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Sugar-free chocolates, sugarless baked snacks, and chewing gums.
additives.notes: A sugar alcohol. Does not promote tooth decay and behaves similarly to sugar in confectionery.

additives.name: Xylitol
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides equal sweetness to sugar with a distinct cooling sensation in the mouth.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Dental chewing gums, toothpastes, mints, and sugar-free throat drops.
additives.notes: A sugar alcohol with proven dental benefits, as mouth bacteria cannot ferment it.

additives.name: Erythritol
additives.primaryPurpose: A non-caloric sugar alcohol used to dilute high-intensity sweeteners.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Diet sodas, sugar-free ice creams, monk fruit blends, and stevia table packs.
additives.notes: Naturally produced by fermenting corn starches. Has a very high digestive tolerance.

additives.name: Polydextroses
additives.primaryPurpose: Replaces the volume and texture of sugar while acting as a soluble dietary fiber.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Low-carb snack bars, sugar-free desserts, and reduced-calorie baked goods.
additives.notes: A highly branched synthetic polymer of glucose with minimal blood sugar impact.

additives.name: Dextrins, roasted starch
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides soluble solids and adhesive properties in food coatings.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Dry seasoning mixes, snack seasonings, pan-coated candies, and batter coatings.
additives.notes: Produced by dry-roasting starch under acidic conditions to break down molecular size.

additives.name: Distarch phosphate
additives.primaryPurpose: Resists structural breakdown during cooking and retort sterilization.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Canned soups, packaged gravies, frozen pies, and dessert puddings.
additives.notes: Starch chemically cross-linked with sodium trimetaphosphate.

additives.name: Acetylated distarch phosphate
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides outstanding freeze-thaw stability and resists retrogradation (water separation).
additives.commonFoodUsage: Frozen dinners, instant sauces, commercial salad dressings, and pie fillings.
additives.notes: Modified food starch that ensures frozen products do not become watery when thawed.

additives.name: Acetylated distarch adipate
additives.primaryPurpose: Modified starch that resists retrogradation (weeping), acid degradation, and high shear forces.
additives.commonFoodUsage: BBQ sauces, commercial gravies, fruit pie fillings, salad dressings, and mayonnaise.
additives.notes: Provides high stability in low-pH (highly acidic) sauces. Ensures the sauce does not separate during freezing or hot-holding cycles.

additives.name: Hydroxypropyl distarch phosphate
additives.primaryPurpose: Provides a smooth, creamy texture in dairy systems; resists acid and heat shearing.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Yogurts, sour creams, commercial custards, canned soups, and baby foods.
additives.notes: A modified starch widely favored in dairy processing for its clean taste and velvety mouthfeel.

additives.name: Starch sodium octenyl succinate
additives.primaryPurpose: Acts as a polymeric emulsifier to encapsulate oil-soluble flavors and vitamins.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Soft drink flavor emulsions, vitamin fortification powders, and salad dressings.
additives.notes: Modified to make the starch molecule partially hydrophobic (oil-attracting).

additives.name: Propylene glycol
additives.primaryPurpose: Dissolves oil-soluble flavor compounds and colors, allowing uniform dispersion.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Liquid food flavorings, liquid food colors, and confectionery coatings.
additives.notes: A clear, odorless liquid. Not to be confused with toxic ethylene glycol.

additives.name: Sorbic acid
additives.primaryPurpose: An organic compound that prevents the growth of molds, yeasts, and fungi.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Grated cheeses, processed cheese spreads, baked goods, and dried fruits.
additives.notes: Highly effective at low levels. Safely halts fungal growth without affecting food aroma or flavor.

additives.name: Calcium sorbate
additives.primaryPurpose: Calcium salt formulation used as an effective surface preservative against mold and yeast.
additives.commonFoodUsage: Pre-shredded/grated cheeses, cheese packaging wraps, and dry bakery glazes.
additives.notes: Frequently utilized in pre-grated cheeses because its physical structure disperses exceptionally evenly.
